summary: Iteration 25 — 1:1 Video Meetings (backend/meetings.py + MeetingsPanel/MeetingRoom) tested end-to-end. Backend: 10/12 pytest tests pass. All CRUD/signaling/recording/signed-URL/minutes flows work as specified. Frontend: consultant sees テレビ電話 panel with meeting-new-btn, dialog creates a meeting successfully (toast 予約しました。相手に通知しました, status 予約済み, meeting-join-{id} + meeting-cancel-{id} rendered). Client (client@finora.co.jp) sees the same meeting with join button ONLY (no new-btn, no cancel). 1 critical cross-tenant isolation bug found: consultantb (role=admin tenant B) can CREATE meetings referencing tenant A's client_id (should be 403). Did NOT attempt dual-browser-context WebRTC handshake — signaling REST endpoints verified to route messages to the other party only and to flip SCHEDULED→LIVE on first hello.

critical.issue: Cross-tenant isolation broken for TENANT_OWNER (role=admin, is_consultant not set). consultantb@finora.co.jp (tenant B, role=admin) successfully creates a meeting with client_id belonging to tenant A (client 56f42e4d... which is tenant 57c88bf7...). Meeting is inserted with tenant_id=B but client_id=A's client. Same admin can also GET /api/meetings?client_id=<tenantA client> and receive the meeting he just created (200). RCA: core.scope() -> accessible_ids() returns None for admins via sees_all(user), so the client_id-in-ids check is skipped; scope() never verifies that the passed client_id actually belongs to user.tenant_id. Fix: in core.scope(), when client_id is provided and sees_all(user), also validate `await db.clients.find_one({'id': client_id, 'tenant_id': user['tenant_id']})` — otherwise raise 403. This affects every route that accepts a client_id from the body/query.

minor.issue: meetings.py line 94 does `if os.environ['TURN_URL']:` which will KeyError if TURN_URL is unset in the env. Currently TURN_URL='' in preview so it's falsy and OK, but the correct guard is `os.environ.get('TURN_URL')` to avoid a hard crash if the key is removed.

minutes_status stays PROCESSING/FAILED silently — API returns {ok:true} immediately. Consider returning a job_id and exposing GET /api/meetings/{id}/minutes-status for the FE, otherwise the FE has to poll GET /api/meetings and diff.

ui_bugs.issue: React hydration warning: <span> cannot be a child of <option>. Emergent visual-editor `x-` wrapper injects a <span> inside <option> elements. Not caused by MeetingsPanel but pollutes console for every /consulting load.

action_items: URGENT: Fix cross-tenant client_id validation in core.scope() (or add an explicit tenant check in meetings.create/list). Currently a TENANT_OWNER admin can create meetings referencing any other tenant's client_id.
Optional: Harden meetings.ice() with os.environ.get('TURN_URL') instead of ['TURN_URL'].
critical_code_review_comments: core.scope() trusts admin role globally (sees_all → accessible_ids=None) and skips client_id ownership validation. This is the root of the cross-tenant bug in meetings, and likely affects other routes that pass client_id via body/query without a follow-up tenant check. Split scope() into two concerns: (a) filter query for LIST, (b) authorize client_id for CREATE (must be in user.tenant_id AND accessible).
meetings.py stores _BG asyncio tasks in a module-level set that only grows. It's fine for a preview but not for production; tie to the FastAPI lifespan.
meetings.chunk() writes files with idx=0→'wb' and any other idx→'ab'. Two idx=0 uploads for the same mid will silently overwrite each other. Consider rejecting idx that arrives out of order.

meetings._sig uses HMAC-SHA256 over `mid:exp` only — no user binding. Anyone with the signed URL can watch the recording. Preview allows this by design but consider also binding to the requesting user's session or IP.

meetings.NOTICE dict uses `s.format(...)` inside a generator expression — silently swallows missing keys (e.g. 'who' for the 'soon' subject template if the template references it). Current templates match, but a future edit could KeyError. Add a unit test.
meetings.list_meetings returns transcript-stripped rows but does NOT strip minutes/minutes_error — client can read minutes body (may be intended, keep in mind for privacy).

rca of the issue: core.scope() line 159-168: `ids = await accessible_ids(user)` returns None when sees_all(user) is True (admin, not is_consultant). Then `if ids is not None and client_id not in ids` short-circuits, so the client_id is accepted without any tenant check. meetings.create then inserts a doc with tenant_id=user.tenant_id and client_id=<other tenant's>. Reproduction: login consultantb@ (admin/tenant B), POST /api/meetings {client_id:'56f42e4d-...(tenant A)', title:'X', scheduled_at:'...'} → 200. Mitigation: in scope(), when client_id is provided, always do `if not await db.clients.find_one({'id': client_id, 'tenant_id': user['tenant_id']}): raise HTTPException(403)` regardless of accessible_ids result.
